claims.text: WhatsApp carries more than 100 billion messages a day (Facebook, Q3 2020 earnings call, 29 Oct 2020; repeated by Meta since)
WhatsApp engineering, Jan 2012: over 2 million TCP connections on a single Erlang/FreeBSD server
Receipts: one grey tick = sent (reached WhatsApp's server), two grey = delivered to the recipient's phone, two blue = read
Messages are stored on WhatsApp's servers only until delivered, then deleted (undelivered ones are kept up to 30 days)
Groups use Sender Keys: the sender encrypts a message once and the server does the fan-out to each member
End-to-end encryption by default since April 2016, built on the Signal Protocol; keys are generated and kept on devices
Attachments are encrypted with a random AES-256 key, uploaded to a blob store; the key, MAC and hash ride in the end-to-end encrypted message
